primary_verdict: externally proved in the exact required form
authentication: Author-hosted Watrous textbook draft and original Bény–Kempf–Kribs arXiv paper read through web retrieval. No external full source retained or redistributed; no content hashes claimed.

checks.source: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, 2018 author-hosted pre-publication draft
checks.locus: Theorem 2.22, printed pp.82–84 / PDF pp.90–92; Theorem 2.26, printed pp.87–89 / PDF pp.95–97
checks.source_result: For finite complex Euclidean spaces, a nonzero map is completely positive iff its Choi matrix is positive iff it has a finite Kraus representation. Trace preservation is equivalent to output partial trace of Choi equal to input identity.
checks.translation: Output tensor input convention matches J(Phi)=sum_ij Phi(E_ij) tensor E_ij. Spectral Choi vectors reshape to Kraus matrices. The zero map is handled separately by an empty or all-zero Kraus family. For CP Kraus, trace preservation is sum K_a* K_a=I.

checks.source: Cédric Bény, Achim Kempf, David W. Kribs, Quantum Error Correction of Observables, arXiv:0705.1574v1
checks.locus: Theorem 9 and Corollary 10, printed pp.10–11; definition of correctability in Section III
checks.source_result: A finite observable subalgebra on PH is correctable for a CPTP channel iff all compressed Kraus products commute with every observable in the algebra.
checks.translation: Source Ea dagger Eb is manuscript Ea*Eb; commutant taken in End(PH). Correctability means one CPTP recovery R with P(E* composed R*)(X)P=X for all algebra observables. This is observable recovery and reduces to scalar Knill–Laflamme for the full corner.

scope: Exact checks of these two external input leaves only. No global novelty search, no reproduction of external proofs, and no certification of infinite-dimensional variants.
